title: Any tutorial or tips for generating character portrait assets?
author: Playful-Jellyfish762
selftext:
Hey, I made a game mainly for myself and it's just a text-based game, but now I kinda want it to have a character portraits. Any tutorial or tips how to generate assets for character portraits? not too complex like having its own different expression, but maybe just a hair swapping and clothes.

I do tried with image edit reference template, but it ended up to be always different and inconsistent in term of position and styles. I was using ChatGPT Image and Nano Banana for this.

I'm not good with English, sorry!

comments.author: MythicScribeDev
comments.body:
When building the portrait generator for my own text-based 5e RPG app, I first used the same basic prompt with different style instructions in order to find the vibe I wanted for the app. When you just ask an image model to swap hair or clothes, or give it different character descriptions without locking down the "camera and lighting rig", the framing, zoom level, and art style drift all over the place.

The one that worked for the style I wanted, and gets appended to the end of every character portrait prompt, is: 'Vertical 3:4 aspect ratio, waist-up portrait, tight chest-up framing, character's head and upper torso centered in frame, cinematic photorealism, 85mm portrait photography, extremely shallow depth of field, highly blurred background, vibrant and colorful lighting, highly detailed textures, warm and cool rim lighting contrast, dynamic composition, Unreal Engine 5 render, fantasy character portrait.'

I use an LLM to take the character's stats/gear/physical description and translate them into a clean, 1-sentence visual description (stripping out game mechanics and focusing only on visible hair, facial features, armor/clothing textures, and setting) starting with "Waist-up portrait of...", and then my backend tacks the styling instructions to the end before sending it to the image generator.

I attached a screenshot below of 9 pre-made characters from my app so you can see how locking the camera framing + lighting wrapper keeps the position and art style super consistent across completely different races, outfits, and backgrounds!
